subject: [PATCH RFC v4 08/12] selftests/mm: cover /proc/pid/mem access to VM_PFNMAP memory

reviews.author: John Hubbard
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that RISC-V architecture uses generic_ioremap_prot(), which does not reject RAM, making the test pass without exercising get_user_page_vma(). He also pointed out that checking byte count is insufficient to distinguish between ->access() and erroneous GUP result for a PFNMAP of normal RAM. Instead, he suggested using a deterministic PFNMAP test provider with mapped page containing one pattern and ->access() callback returning another.

reviewer pointed out that VM_PFNMAP invariant is not correctly described, specifically mentioning that GUP does not return a page for raw mappings, and requested correction in patches 5 and 6; also noted that pread() offsets need to be 64-bit off_t to avoid issues on 32-bit ABIs
reviews.raw_body:
This is architecture-dependent. RISC-V uses generic_ioremap_prot(),
which does not reject RAM, so the old ->access() path can read the COWed
page and this test can pass without exercising get_user_page_vma().

The raw test has the same observability problem: checking only the byte
count cannot distinguish ->access() from an erroneous GUP result for a
PFNMAP of normal RAM. 

Should we instead use a deterministic PFNMAP test provider
whose mapped page contains one pattern and whose ->access() callback
returns another? The COW test could require the anonymous data and the
raw test could require the ->access() pattern. That would also avoid
reading arbitrary MMIO and skipping the raw case in the default run.

---

That is not the VM_PFNMAP invariant. A raw mapping is treated as special
even when its PFN has a valid struct page. Please describe this as GUP
not returning a page for the raw mapping, here and in patches 5 and 6.

The new pread() offsets also need 64-bit off_t. On a 32-bit ABI, a
mapping at or above 2 GiB converts to a negative off_t, and pread64()
rejects it before /proc/self/mem sees the offset.



thanks,
-- 
John Hubbard

2026-07-28.patch_summary: This patch adds two tests to the selftests/mm/pfnmap.c file, which cover accessing VM_PFNMAP memory through /proc/pid/mem. The first test, procmem_cow_read, maps a private and writable file, writes to a copy-on-write (COW) page, and then reads it back through /proc/self/mem. This test ensures that the COW path in get_user_page_vma() works correctly for VM_PFNMAP memory. The second test, procmem_pfn_read, reads a raw physical frame number (PFN) directly through vma->vm_ops->access(), which ioremaps the PFN and rejects RAM pages. This test is skipped for System RAM targets.
